extracted.intended_audience: developers of reporting guidelines, researchers (authors), journal editors, peer-reviewers, and research-funding bodies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for developing, disseminating, implementing, and using reporting guidelines to improve the accuracy and transparency of health-research publications; aimed at authors, editors, peer-reviewers, guideline developers and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reporting items (reporting guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines that specify a minimum set of items for reporting can improve the accuracy and transparency of publications, thus facilitating easier and more reliable appraisal of quality and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established reporting guidelines (e.g., CONSORT, STARD, QUOROM, STROBE) that define the minimum items to be reported for a study type. Such checklists are intended to make reports more complete and appraisable; authors, editors and reviewers should apply them to manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve the accuracy of medical publications (statement: 'improve the accuracy and transparency of publications').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should present methods, results, and interpretations precisely and correctly. Accurate reporting is an essential component of research and not optional; it underpins reliable appraisal and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote transparent reporting so that publications can be reliably appraised for quality and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should disclose study design, conduct, analyses, and any limitations clearly. Transparent reporting enables reproducibility and critical assessment by readers, peer-reviewers, and funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement and support by journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Those guidelines are still not widely supported by medical journals ... Collaboration with and the support of influential medical journals are vital for the success of this project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should endorse relevant reporting guidelines in their instructions to authors and integrate them into editorial and peer-review processes to increase guideline uptake and improve reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence by researchers (authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines are not widely ... adhered to by researchers, and thus their potential impact is lessened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should follow the appropriate reporting guideline for their study type when preparing manuscripts; peer-reviewers and editors should check adherence and request revisions when items are missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust development methods for reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The development methods of most guidelines were broadly similar, but with wide variation in important details. Development usually took a long time and only half the groups had strategies for dissemination and implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers should use explicit, transparent, and consistent methods when creating guidelines, document development processes, plan for evaluation, and include dissemination/implementation strategies from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and implementation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Only half the groups had strategies for dissemination and implementation of their guidelines; lack of dissemination reduces impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline developers must include clear plans for dissemination (e.g., websites, journals, training) and for facilitating adoption by journals, authors, and peer-reviewers; consider tools that help users apply the guideline in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible centralized resources and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: An internet-based resource centre provides a collection of available reporting guidelines and will host other resources ... including a comprehensive digital library, guidance for development, tools to facilitate their use, and educational materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and use centralized, freely accessible repositories (e.g., EQUATOR Network) offering guideline texts, explanatory documents, application tools, and educational material to support authors, editors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for editors, peer-reviewers, and authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Active promotion of such guidelines and their use, by developing and running training for editors, peer-reviewers, and authors. The courses will concentrate on the important factors of research reporting and the efficient use of reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement structured training programs that teach the important aspects of research reporting and how to apply reporting guidelines efficiently in manuscript preparation, editorial decisions, and peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and auditing of guideline implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR network will regularly monitor how journals implement reporting guidelines. We will annually audit the quality of reporting across the health-research literature and hope to document gradual improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish routine monitoring and periodic audits to assess how well journals and authors implement reporting guidelines, track changes in reporting quality over time, and use findings to guide improvement efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient funding for guideline development and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient funding is a necessary requirement for the development and implementation of robust reporting guidelines ... funding bodies' lack of interest in ensuring that this research is reported accurately is deeply disappointing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funders should allocate resources to support the development, assessment, dissemination and implementation of reporting guidelines and related training and monitoring activities; funding is essential to realize guideline impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder collaboration and shared responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor reporting reflects a collective failure of those involved ... EQUATOR's strategic plan reflects the needs of its major stakeholders: developers of reporting guidelines, researchers, journal editors, peer-reviewers, and research-funding bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve reporting through coordinated action among stakeholders (guideline developers, authors, editors, reviewers, funders). Collaboration and engagement of influential journals and institutions are crucial to drive uptake and change practices.
